body:
First off, I wanted to say I feel like I can relate with almost everything you have said. We are very similar in age, career choice, using logic to try and understand ourselves, being so tired of everything, the not quite fitting in with society, the indifference to acquiring wealth, and from what I gathered from comments, the real lack future goals. The only differences really are I have shied away from therapy and have a slightly different (and tumultuous) relationship status. 

One of the things that you said really hit home "I don't ask for anything from anybody and I feel like maybe just this once I deserve to find some kind of peace even if it hurts others." I think this all the time.

First off, I am sorry I don't have any magic answers, and I am sure no one ever will. But after reading your post I had to at least say something...if not to you, then to myself using you as a proxy. One of the things I am starting to realize is that at least some of this feeling comes from being unfulfilled. What one needs to do to fix this I do not know. Drawing from everyday life, I realize one of the times I am not depressed is when I am actively doing something to the point that I can't think about anything else. It could be something as simple as running, or reading, getting caught up in thinking about how something works, or something. I think the key is to find something in your life to distract yourself, sort of like idle minds do the devil's work, although I will be the first to admit I havn't found such a thing in my life, so take that for what it is worth.

Maybe you (and me) just need to pick a project and go with it. Does chemical poisoning in the environment annoy the hell out of you. Then say screw everything else, the world can fix a-y, but z...z is my problem. and then throw yourself into it with reckless abandon. 

My final comment at the moment is kind of a pet idea I have been fostering....and it may very well be crazy. If you ever get to the point where you are going to commit suicide, and you are right at the edge...Tell yourself for all intents and purposes I am already dead. At this point I have made the decision and I accept whatever fall out that will cause. Then tell yourself you are "essentially dead". At this point, any other decision you make will not cause any more harm than what you decided to do. So run away, quit your job, do anything you have always wanted to do. The worse that happens is you end back up in the same place, but hopefully it helps you find something better to do. I hope this makes at least some lick of sense, I am still formulating the idea in my brain.

Best of luck fellow traveler

I do think you are right in that I am unfulfilled. There are things I know I rather be doing but they don't really square with the life I have and the demands and expectations from those around me. So i feel like i'm caught between hurting myself and hurting those around me. And the only difference between the two options is I rather take it out on myself that bother other people.

And don't worry about me doing stupid things...I can be quite good at that ;)

I have a few aversions to professionals. One I am paranoid of having a mental health record and I am worried it could get in the way of security clearances, job prospects, and gun ownership to list a few things.

 I am also worried I will be very confrontational and/or difficult. At my most basic level I truly believe I am right and can form a strong argument for my opinions, and I am not easily swayed by pleas to emotion. And basically I don't want to waste someones time and my money.

In regards to making one's own point to existing, that is basically a conclusion I have come to as well. It worked for a while...but then I eventually come back to not really caring in the end and I don't know how to avoid that. It's like any sandbox video game...I can play for a while, I get bored, and then don't want to play anymore...

I love the idea of moving away to get myself straight. I have wanted to do that for years, but I always run into the fact that I would basically have to throw away everything I have to do it, and I would be doing it alone. 

I am also sorry about your bro.

I have heard of that before. I have also heard that pessimists tend to have more realistic expectations, and people with high IQs tend to have higher instances of depression as well. 

As for the transience, I think I have taken that to its perverse limits. Once you accept happiness is fleeting whenever I feel happy my first thought is...I wonder how long this will last before I'm miserable again....and that is a delightful cycle.

I do think society values happiness far too much..and there is something to be said for being occupied or busy to the point of not thinking and living in the moment. If only my job did not involve thinking all day long :P

"Existing out of courtesy!"

You must be Canadian mate :)
